The answer depends on more than throughput.

Warehouse leaders today are balancing changing demand, labor availability, SKU complexity, and future growth. That means choosing an automation strategy isn't simply about speed. It's about selecting an approach that can adapt as your operation evolves.

• Goods-to-Person (G2P)
• Person-to-Goods (P2G)
• Robots-to-Goods (R2G)

The article explains how each model works, where each delivers the most value, and the operational tradeoffs to consider before investing.

If you're evaluating warehouse automation, this is a useful resource to help frame the conversation.

posts.content:
Walking a tote across the building is not picking work.

But in most operations it takes up a real part of the day. Inventory moving between zones. Parts out to a line. Returns back to processing. Someone carrying a box to a station because there's no faster way to get it there.

Locus robots handle that too. The same fleet doing picking and putaway takes point-to-point moves, scheduled routes on a fixed cadence, and on-demand calls to a station, coordinated with the rest of the work through LocusONE.

One fleet covering more of the workflow, without adding equipment or changing the layout.

For warehouse leaders, it creates a practical path to expand automation beyond assisted picking, increase SKU coverage, and scale execution without redesigning the operation.

posts.content:
Sally Miller, our Global CIO, was recently featured in Fortune talking about what it takes to scale automation and robotics responsibly, in a business as complex and people intensive as ours at DHL Supply Chain.
Across more than 𝟐,𝟖𝟎𝟎 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬, we have deployed over 𝟖,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐨𝐭𝐬. The focus is clear: solve real operational challenges, make work better for our teams and deliver stronger outcomes for our customers.
We only scale what works. This discipline means testing, learning and building solutions that can be rolled out consistently across a global network with long-term partners like Locus Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Robust.AI and SVT Robotics.
What I see in our operations is that automation is delivering tangible impact for our people. Our most advanced sites have lower turnover, faster onboarding and higher employee satisfaction. 
As John Kell points out, as robotics adoption increases, work is evolving. It is shifting toward supervising automated systems and working more closely with vendors to capture data and insights from AI enabled platforms.
We are not just scaling robotics, we are defining how logistics will operate in the future.

Prime Day may dominate retail headlines, but demand spikes aren't limited to a single shopping event.

Recent consumer research from Locus Robotics suggests that online demand is becoming more frequent, more fragmented, and more difficult to predict:

• 72% of consumers make online purchases multiple times per month
• 41% shop online weekly or more often
• 38% decide whether to buy a viral product within 48 hours

For warehouse operations, the challenge is responding to a growing number of demand surges (instead of one peak season) that are driven by promotions, social trends, and shifting consumer behavior throughout the year.

This blog explores what these changes mean for fulfillment operations and why maintaining consistent performance has become increasingly difficult in today's ecommerce environment.

Read the blog: https://lnkd.in/g5zfFDVf
